lesson: Treat failed observation as a request for a changed feasible view or fresh localization.
Preserve successful small retention checks and the measured body envelope; a worst-case freely hanging diameter is not a universal required lift.

No tilted normal is fabricated. Change view; if already over known support with retained bowl, preserve checked lowering and review actual release. Otherwise check return to vacated source and require a changed grasp.

Keep ordinary task decisions. Local motion targets the retained bowl center with free heading and a soft upward-opening objective. Try the Cartesian line first, then obstacle trajectory search; change the local target after failure. Intermediate precision and remaining native steps do not add a task stop.

Allow 10mm estimated RGB-bowl overlap rather than treating every approximate boundary intersection as contact. Raise loaded transit by another 50mm before lateral travel; keep the original final release geometry.

Existing contact is a departure condition, not a reason to block every lift. Keep useful stored geometry when optional refitting fails; positive loss or separate placement still changes the action. A tilted appearance alone never triggers repair; only positive missed placement, overturning, slip or unstable-bottom evidence does. Avoid automatic observation homes; intermediate release must still yield the emptied arm after vertical withdrawal.

Skipping full two-arm home must not leave the empty arm over the receiver. Resolve a short retreat from actual post-withdrawal joints, fall back to one-arm home, and finish that action before the next transfer.

Keep an already nested upper bowl despite mild lean. Occlusion, missing angle/rim measurement and all_stacked=false do not undo a commanded placement. Continue remaining bowls, preserve the release-withdraw-home sequence, and let native termination judge completion; do not repeatedly reseat an uncertain final bowl.
